name: Liverpool

changes.why: On 8 September 2026 the club announced Turkish Airlines (49.12% held by the Turkiye Wealth Fund, a state fund of a Freedom House 'Not Free' country) as front-of-shirt main partner from June 2027; Kevin's rule counts announced plans now, and the original research deferred the drop until the deal starts. Weighed at about half the -1 used for Arsenal's fully state-owned Emirates because the state stake is a minority one.

missing_checked: no FA/UEFA discrimination sanctions on Liverpool fans 2021-26 found (UEFA chant fines found are from 2016)
no current betting partner confirmed (Ladbrokes/Interwetten/Marathonbet deals found are undated or older)
ticket pricing: 3% rise 2026-27 then 2027-28 freeze after Supporters Board talks, already counted in V
1892 Holdings minority deal (Aug 2026): Bhatia left QPR in July 2026, so no multi-club tie found; FSG keeps control
LFC Women in the WSL 2026-27, three Anfield matches, prices frozen: no change
Super League -3 kept: same value as the other five English signatories in scores.py
notes: 1) Check the V move against the original intent: the out/ research listed the Turkish Airlines deal under 'Lowers' but its flag said 'V drops a point when it starts (currently 8, was 9)', which reads as not yet applied. If Kevin takes it as already counted, leave V at 8.2. A full Emirates-style -1 would give 7.2. 2) 1892 Holdings reportedly holds an option to buy a controlling stake within 12 months (Aug 2026 reports, not a formal commitment). If it is exercised, re-check Ownership. Lakshmi Mittal's own QPR shareholding after Bhatia's exit was not verified. 3) A Greek Cypriot supporter's column (Cyprus Mail) objected to the Turkish Airlines deal. No organised fan-group statement (e.g. Spirit of Shankly) was found.

name: Everton

changes.why: In summer 2026 the club renewed Stake on a multi-year deal (sleeve plus stadium and digital presence) as CMC Markets took the shirt front. In February 2025 the Gambling Commission forced Stake out of the GB market and wrote to Everton about the risks of promoting unlicensed gambling sites, which makes this a stronger case than a typical betting sleeve.

missing_checked: multi-club: Friedkin Group still owns AS Roma (and is reported to control Cannes); Multi-club -4 stands. A Sept 2026 report says Friedkin may sell a minority Everton stake to widen the shareholder base, which is not an exit
no FA/UEFA discrimination sanctions on Everton fans 2021-26 found (2023 FA probe concerned Man Utd fans' chant at Lampard)
no state, PE or LBO ownership; Moshiri-era overspend stays dropped (previous owner)
Hill Dickinson Stadium move (2025) already handled by the new-stadium rule in C
front of shirt is now CMC Markets (financial services): neutral
notes: If Roma and Everton ever enter the same UEFA competition, UEFA's multi-club rules could force a structural change. Re-check the multi-club line then.
